signals.title: CAD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Hormuz Reopening
signals.text: CAD/JPY faces intense downside pressure as reports of a Pakistan-mediated deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz trigger a -5.69% collapse in WTI crude prices. This high-impact geopolitical shift reinforces a powerful G10 divergence where JPY is the week's dominant leader (+1.557% avg) while CAD is the primary laggard (-0.882% avg). The pair trades at 112.147, influenced by a massive 2.440% G10 performance spread and a 125bp carry advantage that is failing to provide support against the commodity shock. Positioning is heavily skewed for this reversal, with CAD specs holding a deep net short (16.3% long) while JPY shorts (-124k net) are being forced to cover as safe-haven demand and falling energy costs favor the Yen. This combination of a TIER-1 supply-chain headline and extreme bilateral G10 divergence suggests further CAD/JPY downside as the 'oil-link' breaks. Risk: Negotiations to reopen the Strait fail, sparking a crude price squeeze and CAD recovery.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + Volatility Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY is trading at 157.78, positioned below its SMA20 (162.09), SMA50 (161.28), and SMA200 (157.97) as the technical breakdown accelerates. The options market is signaling extreme caution with a 25d RR at -2.76, the strongest put skew in the G10 space, indicating high demand for USD/JPY downside protection. Interestingly, ATM IV at 7.2% is currently running below HV30 at 8.3%, resulting in a negative Vol Risk Premium of -1.1% which suggests a degree of complacency or thin supply in the vol surface despite the directional skew. The JPY COT LF net short of -124,575 remains a significant fuel source for a further short-squeeze if price sustainedly clears the SMA200 anchor. A 275bp Fed-BoJ carry advantage is currently insufficient to offset the combination of falling crude prices and technical deterioration. Risk: US 10Y yields rebound sharply above 4.75%, reasserting the carry dominance over the JPY haven bid.

signals.title: NZD/USD — COT vs ESI Divergence + RBNZ Hike Bias
signals.text: NZD/USD at 0.5891 continues to trade with a bullish bias, holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.5790–0.5827), yet speculative positioning remains extremely pessimistic. COT LF net short sits at -30,606 with long positioning at a 10-year low of 9.7%, directly contradicting the positive fundamental momentum seen in the NZD Economic Surprise Index (ESI) of +33.4. This divergence is further strained by the RBNZ's hiking stance and a -1.56% real policy rate, which is the most accommodative in the G10 and continues to attract growth-oriented flows. Retail sentiment is also heavily short (74%), creating a multi-layer contrarian setup where both retail and institutional specs are positioned for a decline that the data and price action refuse to deliver. RBNZ holds at 2.5%. Risk: A broad USD rally driven by US 2Y yields moving back toward 4.50% invalidates the NZD-specific squeeze.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Elevated Vol Premium + Carry Advantage
signals.text: AUD/USD is holding at 0.7045, maintaining a position above its SMA20 (0.6980) but encountering resistance near the SMA50 (0.7009). The options market is pricing in significant future turbulence, with an IV of 12.5% against a realized HV30 of 6.5%, creating a notable +6.0% Vol Risk Premium. This elevated premium suggests that despite the 60bp OIS carry advantage AUD holds over the USD (RBA 4.35% vs Fed 3.75%), traders are paying a high price for protection against a trend reversal. The AUD COT positioning is moderately long at +23,616, which aligns with the carry bias but faces headwinds from the negative AUD Economic Surprise Index (-14.7). The 25d RR at -0.64 shows a mild put skew, confirming that the vol premium is skewed toward protecting downside moves rather than chasing the recent 1M +1.86% gain. Risk: RBA shifts to a more dovish tone at the 11 Aug meeting, erasing the carry premium.
